description: We are 404 Brain Not Found, a team from Cochabamba, Bolivia. Our app, Tunari Guard, harmonizes 25 years of NASA MODIS and VIIRS hot spots over Tunari National Park and the city's 15 districts: a comparable activity index, statistical alerts, a real-time map and an AI assistant. We are developers and data analysts (NestJS, PostGIS, Angular, Python). Our team is complete, but we welcome feedback from fire experts.
summary:
Tunari Guard is a web platform that monitors heat hotspots in Tunari National Park and the 15 districts of Cochabamba, Bolivia, using 25 years of NASA satellite data.

The challenge: the MODIS (since 2001) and VIIRS (since 2012) sensors have different resolutions, and VIIRS detects almost three times more, so their data cannot be compared directly. Tunari Guard harmonizes them into a single index that shows whether one year was truly more active than another.

What it offers:
- Interactive map of detections with filters, custom drawn areas and data downloads.
- Monthly history and thermal calendar since 2001.
- Statistical alerts for unusually active months.
- Real-time alerts: every 10 minutes it checks NASA data and flags new hotspots in the area.
- Tuni, an AI assistant that answers questions about the data in plain language.
- Reports and projections to support fire prevention planning.

A satellite heat detection is not a confirmed fire: the platform states this clearly and separates real, provisional and simulated data.

Built by 404 Brain Not Found for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Tunari Guard turns 25 years of NASA FIRMS hotspot detections into clear, comparable information for Tunari National Park and the 15 districts of Cochabamba, Bolivia, an area hit by wildfires every dry season.

HOW IT WORKS

MODIS (2001 onward, 1 km) and VIIRS (2012 onward, 375 m) cannot be compared directly: VIIRS detects about 2.9 times more. We count "cell-days" on a 1 km grid, so one fire seen by two satellites is not counted twice, and convert VIIRS to the MODIS scale with a factor calibrated in Tunari (2013-2025). The result is a single harmonized monthly index from 2001 to today. A statistical model compares each month with its own history and flags unusual activity, with probabilities and a plain-language reading. Every 10 minutes the backend downloads new NASA FIRMS detections, filters the study area, assigns each one to its district with PostGIS and pushes new hotspots and prioritized alerts to every open screen in real time.

BENEFITS

- One trustworthy view of fire activity across 25 years and two sensors.

- Real-time alerts for park rangers and local authorities.

- Open data: filter, draw any area on the map and download CSV or GeoJSON.

- Tuni, an AI assistant that answers questions about the data in plain Spanish, with voice support, using only verified data from the platform.

INTENDED IMPACT

Help authorities, rangers, researchers and citizens see where and when fires concentrate, detect unusual seasons early and plan prevention with evidence instead of guesses.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

- Data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1, VIIRS Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21), open district and park boundaries.

- Data science: Python notebooks for harmonization, negative binomial alert model, hotspot clustering (Getis-Ord Gi*) and trend tests (Mann-Kendall).

- Backend: TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL with PostGIS, Prisma, Socket.IO, MinIO.

- Frontend: Angular, Leaflet maps, ECharts, Tailwind CSS.

- AI: OpenAI API for the Tuni chat, speech-to-text and text-to-speech.

- Deployment: Docker Compose and Caddy with automatic HTTPS on a VPS.

CREATIVITY

We combined scientific harmonization with an accessible experience: a thermal calendar that shows 25 years at a glance, live alerts, a replay mode that reproduces past fire seasons as if they were happening now, and Tuni, a friendly mascot who explains satellite data to non-experts.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Scientific honesty: a heat detection is not a confirmed fire, and the platform says so everywhere.

- Uncertainty: we show data quality and keep real, provisional (NRT) and simulated data clearly separated.

- Local context: Bolivia time zone, Spanish interface and non-official boundaries labeled as such.

- Reliability: duplicate-free imports, validation against documented fire cases and an architecture ready to scale.
